figures.finding: The Film Development Council's Film Location Incentive Program (FLIP) is a selective cash rebate of 20% on eligible spend, up to PHP 25 million, for international projects that engage a Philippine company for line production, animation or post-production; a 5% cultural bonus raises the total to PHP 30 million. Its International Co-Production Fund (ICOF) gives up to PHP 10 million to co-productions (cultural bonus up to PHP 2 million; ASEAN co-productions PHP 1 million more).

value.name: Film Location Incentive Program (FLIP)
value.recipient: Philippine production company / audiovisual service provider

sources.said: FLIP provides a 20% cash rebate of up to ₱25 million ($424,000) for eligible international projects in partnership with Filipino audiovisual service providers, while projects that prominently showcase Filipino culture and creativity may also qualify for a 5% cultural bonus, increasing total rebate to ₱30 million ($508,000). Meanwhile, ICOF offers up to ₱10 million ($169,000) to projects co-produced with the Philippines. Qualified projects may also receive a cultural bonus of up to ₱2 million ($34,000), while ASEAN co-productions are guaranteed an additional ₱1 million ($17,000).

The Film Location Incentive Program (FLIP) is a selective cash rebate program provided by the Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP), through the Film Philippines Office (FPO). It supports international audiovisual projects that engage a Philippine production company to undertake line production, animation, and/or post-production services in the Philippines.

figures.finding: The Film Development Council of the Philippines' local fund, CreatePHFilms, gives selected Filipino projects a fixed PHP 1 million for a film budgeted under PHP 15 million, PHP 3 to 5 million for one of PHP 15 million or more, up to PHP 500,000 for development (raised from PHP 300,000 in 2026), PHP 300,000 to 500,000 for post-production and up to PHP 500,000 for a short; Cycle 1 of 2026 (applications 6 to 23 February 2026) selected five development projects, one small-budget and three large-budget productions and the short films.
figures.applies: Philippines, Filipino filmmakers, 2025 Cycle 2 and 2026 Cycle 1.
